lines.text: The wire went into the wall.
And stopped.
The gauge was never connected to *anything.*
Someone made that needle point to zero.
Which meant that behind Hatch 3, there might be air.
And someone might be *alive.*
Someone who had knocked for thirty nights. And then stopped.
I called Ground. Ground, the Hatch 3 gauge is fake.
Ground copies. Continue.
Day ninety. Envelope three.
Channel 9. Don't answer. Whatever it says.
He underlined it twice.
Why would Hale write the same rule twice?
Unless he knew something was going to call.
Hale wrote rule one. Never open Hatch 3.
Hale wrote: trust the numbers.
Did Hale *know?*
And if he knew, why did he leave me here?
Every night, I pressed my ear to the hatch.
Nothing. No knocks. Just the fans.
Day one hundred. I circled a date on the calendar.
Day 186. The day the oxygen runs out.
Eighty-six days away. The ship was 265 days away.
Every number on that station was counting down.
Day one hundred four. Seven in the evening.
A light came on that I had never seen lit before.
Channel 9.
Ground had never used channel 9.
The radio clicked. And a voice said:
This is Ground. *Open* *Hatch* *3.*
